# PsyConnect

> consciousness, connection, ceremony & psychedelics — in person in london. Gathered daily from the hosts' own listings; every event has its own page with the date, venue, price and a link to book.

- [What's on — all upcoming events](https://psyconnect.london/)
- [Tonight](https://psyconnect.london/tonight/)
- [This weekend](https://psyconnect.london/this-weekend/)

## Practices

- [Ecstatic dance in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/ecstatic-dance/): Ecstatic dance is a freeform dance floor with no talking, no alcohol and no steps to learn.
- [5Rhythms classes in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/5rhythms/): 5Rhythms is a moving meditation created by Gabrielle Roth: every class travels through flowing, staccato, chaos, lyrical and stillness, a wave that takes about two hours.
- [Sound baths, gong baths & sound healing in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/sound-bath/): A sound bath is an hour lying on the floor while someone plays gongs, singing bowls, chimes and voice around the room.
- [Cacao ceremonies & cacao circles in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/cacao-ceremony/): A cacao ceremony is a gathering where everyone drinks a cup of thick, bitter ceremonial cacao together and then sits, moves or shares for a couple of hours.
- [Breathwork classes & workshops in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/breathwork/): Breathwork is a session where a facilitator guides you through a specific breathing pattern — usually connected, mouth-led and faster than normal — while you lie down with music playing.
- [Somatic workshops & embodiment in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/somatics/): Somatic work starts from the body rather than the story: slow movement, attention to sensation, and pauses long enough to notice what shifts.
- [Qigong classes in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/qigong/): Qigong is a Chinese practice of slow, repeated movement coordinated with breath and attention.
- [Tantra workshops & classes in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/tantra/): Tantra workshops in London are mostly neo-tantra: a modern, Western take on the Indian tradition that works with breath, slow touch, eye contact and attention to build intimacy — with yourself, a partner or a room of strangers.
- [Family constellations workshops in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/family-constellations/): Family constellations is a group process developed by Bert Hellinger.
- [Authentic relating & circling in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/authentic-relating/): Authentic relating is a set of guided conversation practices for meeting people honestly: saying what is actually true for you in the moment, and getting curious about the person in front of you instead of performing.
- [Contact improvisation jams & classes in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/contact-improvisation/): Contact improvisation is a movement practice built on a shared point of contact: two people lean, roll, lift and give weight, following momentum rather than choreography.
- [Bohm dialogue groups in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/bohm-dialogue/): A Bohm dialogue is a group conversation with no agenda, no leader and nothing to decide.
- [Kirtan & chanting circles in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/kirtan/): Kirtan is call-and-response chanting from the Indian devotional tradition: a leader sings a line of a mantra, usually with harmonium and drum, and the room sings it back, slowly at first and then faster until it lifts.
- [Shamanic journeys, drumming & trance dance in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/shamanic/): Shamanic sessions use rhythm, breath and ritual to reach an altered, dreamlike state without substances.
- [Sufi whirling & Sufi meditation in London](https://psyconnect.london/p/sufi-whirling/): Sufi whirling, or turning, is the moving meditation of the Mevlevi order founded after the 13th-century poet Rumi: you turn slowly on the spot, right hand raised and left lowered, keeping a still centre as the room spins around you.

## Through the year

- [Winter solstice gatherings in London](https://psyconnect.london/winter-solstice/): The winter solstice, around 21 December, is the longest night of the year: from here the days start getting longer again.
- [New Year's Eve & New Year ceremonies in London](https://psyconnect.london/new-year/): Not everyone wants to see the year in at a bar.
- [Valentine's Day events for connection in London](https://psyconnect.london/valentines/): An alternative to a set menu: Valentine's week in London brings tantra and couples' workshops, slow-dating and speed-dating nights, cuddle parties, cacao ceremonies, heart-opening sound baths and authentic relating evenings, whether you go as a couple, with friends or on your own.
- [Spring equinox gatherings in London](https://psyconnect.london/spring-equinox/): The spring equinox, around 20 March, is when day and night are of equal length and the light starts to win.
- [Beltane & May Day celebrations in London](https://psyconnect.london/beltane/): Beltane, on 1 May, is the old Celtic fire festival of summer's start: fertility, flowers, maypoles and bonfires.
- [Summer solstice gatherings in London](https://psyconnect.london/summer-solstice/): The summer solstice, around 21 June, is the longest day of the year.
- [Autumn equinox gatherings in London](https://psyconnect.london/autumn-equinox/): The autumn equinox, around 22 September, balances day and night before the dark half of the year.
- [Samhain & Halloween gatherings in London](https://psyconnect.london/samhain/): Samhain, on the night of 31 October, is the Celtic new year and the root of Halloween: the time when the veil between the living and the dead is said to be thinnest.
